paper.title: Testing the decoy effect to improve online survey participation: Evidence from a field experiment
paper.description: Does adding a less attractive survey option increase actual completion of the original survey, and does its position in the invitation matter?

review.reason: Accepted exact candidate as a concise reading-only research summary with source locators and explicit scope limits. This is not full-instrument or executable-protocol approval.
checks: Compared main article and supplement with two reading scopes, delivered invitations, actual completion and randomized presentation order; six decoy completions count as non-target.
Checked Fig.2/prose preference conflict and Table2/prose pooled-rate conflict, plus order-specific rates and adjusted odds ratios. Summary does not equate simulated choice with field completion.
Recomputed exact asset digest; inspected only Program and source manifest are included. No protocol, participant records, original PDF, credentials or executable materials included.
Independently re-reviewed added headline takeaway and prediction nodes against the already inspected primary source and rebound this acceptance to the refreshed full asset digest.
review.reviewScope: Primary-source comparison of the claims actually present in this concise reading summary, citation section/table locators, and public-asset privacy. Not exhaustive extraction, reanalysis, runtime testing, or historical-fidelity certification.
review.sourceAccessNote: Original documents were reviewed locally using extracted text/OCR, and for study_016 via the author-uploaded publisher article on ResearchGate. Sources remain external; acceptance does not guarantee access without a library subscription or permanent availability of links.
